plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so bidding above value risks overpaying, and bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $15, I should bid exactly $15 to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I win whenever it's profitable (my value exceeds the second-highest bid) and lose when it wouldn't be profitable.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (equal to my value) is the dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding my true value of $36 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable) and lose when it doesn't (avoiding losses). There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down since I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid.

This is a second-price auction (highest bidder pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $42.
